rationale:
The selected node is the conjunction of three independent theorems from Simon §2 (Theorem 2.6, Lemma 2.7, Lemma 2.8). Its proof is therefore the anonymous constructor ⟨Submission.bv_compactness_theorem, Submission.bv_poincare_theorem, Submission.bv_extension_estimate_theorem⟩, and this assembly was type-checked in Lean against BVCompactness ∧ BVPoincare ∧ BVExtensionEstimate. All three supplied proofs rest on the mollification toolkit of Section T, which is the content of Simon's Lemma 2.5. Leaving the toolkit inside the conjuncts would make each of them re-prove the hardest analytic steps, so the toolkit is split out.

The split has 8 children.
- Three shared tools:
  - (1) bv_lipschitz_integration_by_parts (T3), used by children 3 and 5;
  - (2) bv_mollifier_tendsto_L1 (T2), used by children 4, 5 and 7;
  - (3) bv_mollifier_fderiv_lintegral_le (T4–T6, the gradient bound of 2.5), used by children 4, 5 and 7.
- Two key estimates, each feeding one conjunct:
  - (4) bv_mollifier_sub_lintegral_le (T7), the uniform L¹ mollification error behind 2.6;
  - (5) bv_abs_variation_le (T8), |D|u|| ≤ |Du|, the step “by 2.5 and lower semicontinuity” in 2.8.
- The three conjuncts (6)–(8), with their exact frozen types and the parent's Section A/B/C proofs, now citing the tools. Each may split further at the next depth (diagonal extraction, convex Poincaré, distance-function cut-offs).
The DAG is acyclic: 1, 2 → 3 → 4, 5; 4 → 6; 2, 3 → 7; 5 → 8.

Changes to the toolkit statements relative to Section T.
- ContDiffBump.normed is outside the frozen import closure: Lean rejects `.normed` after `import GMT.Ch02.Submission`. So every mollifier statement quantifies over an arbitrary kernel ρ with these properties: continuous (T2, T7) or C² (T6), nonnegative, ∫ρ = 1, support ρ ⊆ ball 0 σ. A Lean check confirms that normalized bumps satisfy these hypotheses.
- The symmetry φ(−x) = φ(x) is dropped; the proof uses the reflected kernel instead.
- The inner parallel set W^(σ) becomes the hypothesis ∀ x ∈ K, closedBall x σ ⊆ W. This covers every use (B3, T7, T8).
- T7's margin Q + B̄(0,3σ) ⊆ W is relaxed to closedBall x σ ⊆ W for x ∈ Q, because the proof only uses ‖z‖ < σ on the support of ρ.
- Derivatives appear only as fderiv, because gradient is not in the frozen closure.
Proofs may add Mathlib imports, for example BumpFunction.Normed, Convex.Measure and ContinuousMapDense.

It covered n = 0, empty or whole W, non-measurable K, infinite variation and Bochner junk values. subproblems.title: Integration by parts against a compactly supported Lipschitz vector field
subproblems.statement: For every n ∈ ℕ, every C¹ function F : ℝⁿ → ℝ (ℝⁿ = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n)), every K ∈ ℝ≥0 and every K-Lipschitz vector field g : ℝⁿ → ℝⁿ with compact support, ∫_{ℝⁿ} F(x)·div g(x) dx = −∫_{ℝⁿ} DF(x)[g(x)] dx, where div g(x) = trace Dg(x) is SimonGMT Chapter02.euclideanDivergence g x (Dg = Mathlib fderiv, which is 0 at points of non-differentiability), DF(x) = fderiv ℝ F x, and both integrals are Bochner integrals for Lebesgue measure (volume).
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (n : ℕ) (F : Rn n → ℝ) (g : Rn n → Rn n) (K : ℝ≥0), ContDiff ℝ 1 F → LipschitzWith K g → HasCompactSupport g → ∫ x, F x * Chapter02.euclideanDivergence g x = -∫ x, fderiv ℝ F x (g x)
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: parent proof, Section T, step T3 (integration by parts for Lipschitz functions), which the parent uses inside T5 (smooth duality) and T8 (|D|u|| ≤ |Du|). It is the Fubini / absolute-continuity-on-lines step of Simon's printed proof of Rademacher's theorem (Ch. 2, 1.4), available in Mathlib as LipschitzWith.integral_lineDeriv_mul_eq.

Notation. E := ℝⁿ = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n) and μ := volume, Lebesgue measure, which is an additive Haar measure. All integrals are Bochner integrals over E with respect to μ. For a map h on E, Dh(x) := fderiv ℝ h x is Mathlib's totalized derivative (0 where h is not differentiable). div g(x) := Chapter02.euclideanDivergence g x = trace Dg(x). (e_i)_{i ∈ Fin n} is the standard orthonormal basis of E (stdOrthonormalBasis ℝ E, or EuclideanSpace.single i 1). Fix n, F ∈ C¹(E), K ≥ 0 and a K-Lipschitz g : E → E with compact support. Put S := tsupport g, which is compact.

1. Facts about div g.
 (a) div g is Borel measurable (SimonGMT measurable_euclideanDivergence).
 (b) |div g(x)| ≤ n·K for every x (SimonGMT norm_euclideanDivergence_le_of_lipschitz; finrank ℝ E = n).
 (c) div g(x) = 0 for x ∉ S (SimonGMT support_euclideanDivergence_subset).
 (d) For every orthonormal basis b of E and every x, div g(x) = Σ_i ⟨b_i, Dg(x) b_i⟩ (SimonGMT euclideanDivergence_eq_sum_inner). This holds at every x, including points where Dg(x) = 0 by convention.

2. Both integrands are integrable.
 - F is continuous, hence bounded on the compact set S by some A ≥ 0. By 1(b) and 1(c), |F(x) div g(x)| ≤ A·n·K·1_S(x). Also F·div g is measurable (continuous times Borel). Since μ(S) < ∞, F·div g ∈ L¹(μ).
 - The map x ↦ DF(x)[g(x)] is continuous: DF is continuous because F is C¹, g is continuous, and evaluation is continuous. It vanishes outside S because g(x) = 0 there. So it is continuous with compact support, hence integrable.

3. Reduction to a globally Lipschitz, compactly supported F̃.
 Choose R₀ > 0 with S ⊆ B(0,R₀) (S is bounded). Take a C^∞ function χ : E → [0,1] with compact support and χ = 1 on closedBall(0,R₀); for example the ContDiffBump centred at 0 with rIn = R₀ and rOut = R₀ + 1 (Mathlib ContDiffBump.contDiff, ContDiffBump.one_of_mem_closedBall, ContDiffBump.hasCompactSupport, values in [0,1]).
 Put F̃ := χ·F. Then F̃ is C¹ with compact support, hence Lipschitz (Mathlib ContDiff.lipschitzWith_of_hasCompactSupport).
 On the open set N := B(0,R₀) ⊇ S we have F̃ = F, so DF̃(x) = DF(x) for every x ∈ N (functions that agree on a neighbourhood have the same derivative). Consequently, for every x:
 - F̃(x) div g(x) = F(x) div g(x): on S because F̃ = F there, and off S both sides vanish by 1(c);
 - DF̃(x)[g(x)] = DF(x)[g(x)]: on S ⊆ N the derivatives agree, and off S, g(x) = 0.
 Hence it suffices to prove ∫ F̃ div g = −∫ DF̃(x)[g(x)] dx.

4. Coordinatewise integration by parts.
 For i ∈ Fin n let g_i(x) := ⟨e_i, g(x)⟩. Each g_i is K-Lipschitz (|⟨e_i, a − b⟩| ≤ ‖a − b‖) and has compact support (support g_i ⊆ support g). Mathlib LipschitzWith.integral_lineDeriv_mul_eq, applied with f := F̃, g := g_i, v := e_i and μ = volume, gives
   ∫ lineDeriv ℝ F̃ x e_i · g_i(x) dx = ∫ lineDeriv ℝ g_i x (−e_i) · F̃(x) dx.   (∗_i)

5. Identification of the integrands.
 (a) F̃ is differentiable everywhere, so lineDeriv ℝ F̃ x e_i = DF̃(x)[e_i] for every x (Mathlib DifferentiableAt.lineDeriv_eq_fderiv).
 (b) By Rademacher's theorem (Mathlib LipschitzWith.ae_differentiableAt), g is differentiable at μ-a.e. x. At such x, g_i = (innerSL ℝ e_i) ∘ g is differentiable with Dg_i(x)[v] = ⟨e_i, Dg(x)[v]⟩. Hence lineDeriv ℝ g_i x (−e_i) = Dg_i(x)[−e_i] = −⟨e_i, Dg(x) e_i⟩.
 By integral_congr_ae, (∗_i) therefore becomes
   ∫ DF̃(x)[e_i]·⟨e_i, g(x)⟩ dx = −∫ ⟨e_i, Dg(x) e_i⟩·F̃(x) dx.   (∗∗_i)
 Both integrands in (∗∗_i) are integrable:
 - the left one is continuous with compact support;
 - the right one is measurable (x ↦ Dg(x) e_i is measurable, Mathlib measurable_fderiv_apply_const), bounded by K·sup|F̃|, and vanishes off S (Dg(x) = 0 for x ∉ tsupport g, Mathlib fderiv_of_notMem_tsupport).

6. Summation over i.
 For every x, Σ_i DF̃(x)[e_i]·⟨e_i, g(x)⟩ = DF̃(x)[Σ_i ⟨e_i, g(x)⟩ e_i] = DF̃(x)[g(x)], by linearity and the orthonormal expansion g(x) = Σ_i ⟨e_i, g(x)⟩ e_i. Also Σ_i ⟨e_i, Dg(x) e_i⟩ = div g(x) by 1(d).
 Summing (∗∗_i) over the finite set Fin n, using additivity of the integral for integrable functions (Mathlib integral_finsetSum), gives
   ∫ DF̃(x)[g(x)] dx = −∫ F̃(x) div g(x) dx.

7. By step 3, ∫ F div g = ∫ F̃ div g = −∫ DF̃(x)[g(x)] dx = −∫ DF(x)[g(x)] dx. ∎

Remark (n = 0). E is a single point, so g ≡ 0, Dg = 0 and DF = 0. Both sides vanish, and the argument above also covers this case (all sums are empty).
proof_key_steps: div g is Borel, bounded by n·K and vanishes off tsupport g (SimonGMT lemmas), so F·div g and x ↦ DF(x)[g(x)] are integrable.
Replace F by F̃ = χF with χ ∈ C_c^∞ equal to 1 near tsupport g; F̃ is Lipschitz and both integrands are unchanged.
For each coordinate g_i = ⟨e_i, g⟩ apply Mathlib LipschitzWith.integral_lineDeriv_mul_eq with v = e_i.
Identify the line derivatives a.e. with fderiv: everywhere for F̃, and by Rademacher (LipschitzWith.ae_differentiableAt) for g.
Sum over the orthonormal basis: Σ DF̃[e_i]⟨e_i,g⟩ = DF̃[g] and Σ⟨e_i, Dg e_i⟩ = div g (euclideanDivergence_eq_sum_inner).

subproblems.title: L¹ convergence of mollifications with shrinking supports
subproblems.statement: For every n ∈ ℕ, every F ∈ L¹(ℝⁿ) (Integrable F volume), every sequence of kernels ρ_j : ℝⁿ → ℝ (j ∈ ℕ) that are continuous, nonnegative, satisfy support ρ_j ⊆ B(0,σ_j) (open ball) and ∫ρ_j = 1, and every sequence σ_j → 0: ∫⁻_{ℝⁿ} |(ρ_j * F)(x) − F(x)| dx → 0 in [0,∞], where (ρ_j * F)(x) := convolution (ρ j) F (lsmul ℝ ℝ) volume x = ∫ ρ_j(t) F(x − t) dt.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (n : ℕ) (F : Rn n → ℝ) (ρ : ℕ → Rn n → ℝ) (σ : ℕ → ℝ), Integrable F volume → (∀ j, Continuous (ρ j)) → (∀ j x, 0 ≤ ρ j x) → (∀ j, Function.support (ρ j) ⊆ ball 0 (σ j)) → (∀ j, ∫ x, ρ j x = 1) → Tendsto σ atTop (𝓝 0) → Tendsto (fun j ↦ ∫⁻ x, ‖convolution (ρ j) F (ContinuousLinearMap.lsmul ℝ ℝ) volume x - F x‖ₑ) atTop (𝓝 0)
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: parent proof, Section T, step T2 (L¹ convergence of mollifiers). The parent uses it in T7, T8 and B4, and it is the “convergence in L¹_loc is standard” part of Simon's printed Lemma 2.5. Here it is stated for an arbitrary sequence of continuous, nonnegative, normalized kernels with shrinking supports, instead of the dilates φ_σ of one fixed mollifier; the argument is the same.

Notation. E := ℝⁿ = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n) and μ := volume (Lebesgue measure; it is invariant under translations and under x ↦ −x). For G : E → ℝ, (ρ_j * G)(x) := convolution (ρ j) G (lsmul ℝ ℝ) volume x = ∫ ρ_j(t)·G(x − t) dt, by definition of Mathlib's convolution. ‖·‖₁ denotes ∫⁻ |·| dμ ∈ [0,∞].

1. Properties of the kernels.
 Since ∫ρ_j = 1 ≠ 0, the function ρ_j is not identically 0, so B(0,σ_j) ≠ ∅ and σ_j > 0. Because ρ_j is continuous with support in B(0,σ_j), we have tsupport ρ_j ⊆ closedBall(0,σ_j), which is compact. Hence ρ_j is bounded and integrable, and ∫|ρ_j| = ∫ρ_j = 1.

2. Pointwise existence, linearity and the L¹ contraction.
 Let G ∈ L¹(μ). For every x, t ↦ G(x − t) is integrable (μ is invariant under t ↦ x − t) and ρ_j is bounded and measurable. So t ↦ ρ_j(t)G(x − t) is integrable, and (ρ_j * G)(x) is an absolutely convergent integral. In particular G ↦ (ρ_j * G)(x) is linear on L¹.
 Moreover, by Tonelli and translation invariance,
   ∫⁻ |(ρ_j * G)(x)| dx ≤ ∫⁻∫⁻ ρ_j(t)|G(x − t)| dt dx = ∫⁻ ρ_j(t) (∫⁻ |G(x − t)| dx) dt = (∫ρ_j)·‖G‖₁ = ‖G‖₁.
 The joint measurability of (x,t) ↦ ρ_j(t)|G(x − t)| holds because G is a.e.-strongly measurable and (x,t) ↦ x − t is quasi-measure-preserving (Mathlib AEStronglyMeasurable.comp_quasiMeasurePreserving / quasiMeasurePreserving_sub).

3. Approximation of F. Fix ε > 0 (real). By density of continuous compactly supported functions in L¹ (Mathlib Integrable.exists_hasCompactSupport_lintegral_sub_le), choose F₀ : E → ℝ continuous with compact support such that ∫⁻ |F − F₀| ≤ ofReal ε. Then F − F₀ ∈ L¹, and by step 2, ∫⁻ |ρ_j * (F − F₀)| ≤ ofReal ε for every j.

4. Uniform approximation of F₀.
 Let S := tsupport F₀ + closedBall(0,1). It is compact (a sum of compact sets), so μ(S) < ∞. Put ε' := ε/(μ(S).toReal + 1) > 0.
 F₀ is uniformly continuous (continuous with compact support), so choose r ∈ (0,1] with |F₀(y) − F₀(y')| ≤ ε' whenever ‖y − y'‖ < r. Since σ_j → 0, there is J with σ_j < r for all j ≥ J.
 Fix j ≥ J and x ∈ E. Since ∫ρ_j = 1,
   (ρ_j * F₀)(x) − F₀(x) = ∫ ρ_j(t)(F₀(x − t) − F₀(x)) dt,
 and ρ_j(t) ≠ 0 only when ‖t‖ < σ_j < r. Hence |(ρ_j * F₀)(x) − F₀(x)| ≤ ∫ ρ_j(t)·ε' dt = ε'.
 If x ∉ S, then for ‖t‖ < 1 the point x − t is not in tsupport F₀ (otherwise x = (x − t) + t ∈ S). So F₀(x − t) = 0 whenever ρ_j(t) ≠ 0, and also F₀(x) = 0; hence (ρ_j * F₀)(x) − F₀(x) = 0.
 Therefore ∫⁻ |ρ_j * F₀ − F₀| ≤ ofReal(ε')·μ(S) ≤ ofReal ε for all j ≥ J.

5. Triangle inequality. By step 2 (linearity), ρ_j * F − ρ_j * F₀ = ρ_j * (F − F₀) pointwise. So for every x,
   |(ρ_j * F)(x) − F(x)| ≤ |(ρ_j * (F − F₀))(x)| + |(ρ_j * F₀)(x) − F₀(x)| + |F₀(x) − F(x)|.
 Integrate with ∫⁻; the lower integral is monotone and additive for a.e.-measurable functions, and all three terms are a.e.-measurable. Using steps 3 and 4, for all j ≥ J:
   ∫⁻ |ρ_j * F − F| ≤ ofReal ε + ofReal ε + ofReal ε = ofReal(3ε).

6. Conclusion. For every real ε > 0 the [0,∞]-valued sequence a_j := ∫⁻ |ρ_j * F − F| eventually satisfies a_j ≤ ofReal(3ε). Hence a_j → 0 (ENNReal.tendsto_nhds_zero; ε is arbitrary). This is the claim. ∎

Remark (n = 0). E is a point of measure 1 and (ρ_j * F)(0) = ρ_j(0)F(0) = F(0), so a_j = 0. The general argument covers this case too.
proof_key_steps: ∫ρ_j = 1 forces σ_j > 0; ρ_j is bounded, compactly supported and integrable.
Young/Tonelli contraction: ‖ρ_j * G‖₁ ≤ ‖G‖₁ for G ∈ L¹, and convolution is linear in G.
Density: choose F₀ ∈ C_c with ‖F − F₀‖₁ ≤ ε (Integrable.exists_hasCompactSupport_lintegral_sub_le).
Uniform continuity: ρ_j * F₀ → F₀ uniformly with support in tsupport F₀ + closedBall(0,1), hence in L¹.
Triangle inequality gives limsup ‖ρ_j * F − F‖₁ ≤ 3ε for every ε, hence convergence to 0.

subproblems.title: Gradient bound for mollified functions on inner parallel sets (Simon 2.5)
subproblems.statement: For every n ∈ ℕ, every open W ⊆ ℝⁿ, every set K ⊆ ℝⁿ, every u integrable on W, every σ ∈ ℝ and every kernel ρ : ℝⁿ → ℝ of class C² with ρ ≥ 0, support ρ ⊆ B(0,σ) (open ball) and ∫ρ = 1, if closedBall(x,σ) ⊆ W for every x ∈ K then, with w := ρ * (1_W u) (Mathlib convolution ρ (W.indicator u) (lsmul ℝ ℝ) volume, i.e. w(x) = ∫ ρ(t)(1_W u)(x − t) dt), ∫⁻_K ‖Dw(x)‖ dx ≤ |Du|(W) := SimonGMT bvVariationOn u W in [0,∞]; here Dw = fderiv ℝ w and ‖·‖ is the operator norm.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (n : ℕ) (W K : Set (Rn n)) (u ρ : Rn n → ℝ) (σ : ℝ), IsOpen W → IntegrableOn u W volume → ContDiff ℝ 2 ρ → (∀ x, 0 ≤ ρ x) → Function.support ρ ⊆ ball 0 σ → ∫ x, ρ x = 1 → (∀ x ∈ K, closedBall x σ ⊆ W) → ∫⁻ x in K, ‖fderiv ℝ (convolution ρ (W.indicator u) (ContinuousLinearMap.lsmul ℝ ℝ) volume) x‖ₑ ≤ Chapter02.bvVariationOn u W
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: parent proof, Section T, steps T4 (variation of a mollification), T5 (smooth duality) and T6 (gradient bound: ∫_{W^(σ)} |∇(φ_σ*(u1_W))| ≤ |Du|(W)). These carry out the computation in Simon's printed proof of Lemma 2.5:
“for fixed smooth g with |g| ≤ f and σ < dist(spt f, ∂U): ∫ g·∇u_(σ) = −∫ u_(σ) div g = −∫ φ_σ * u div g = −∫ u φ_σ * div g = −∫ u div(φ_σ * g)”, together with “(4) ∫ f|Du_(σ)| = sup_{|g|≤f, g smooth} ∫ g·∇u_(σ)”.
Two adaptations: the fixed mollifier φ_σ is replaced by an arbitrary C² kernel ρ ≥ 0 with ∫ρ = 1 and support in B(0,σ) (no symmetry is assumed; the reflected kernel ρ̌ is used instead), and the inner parallel set W^(σ) is replaced by the hypothesis “closedBall(x,σ) ⊆ W for x ∈ K”.

Notation. E := ℝⁿ = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n), μ := volume (Lebesgue measure, invariant under translations and under x ↦ −x). Dh(x) := fderiv ℝ h x. div h := Chapter02.euclideanDivergence h = trace Dh. |Du|(W) := Chapter02.bvVariationOn u W is the supremum, over g ∈ C_c(E,E) that are Lipschitz (IsLipschitzTestField) with tsupport g ⊆ W and compactlySupportedSupNorm g ≤ 1, of ofReal(∫_W u div g).

0. Preliminaries.
 - F := 1_W u = W.indicator u. W is open, hence measurable, so F ∈ L¹(E) (integrable_indicator_iff).
 - Since ∫ρ = 1, we have ρ ≢ 0, so B(0,σ) ≠ ∅ and σ > 0. tsupport ρ ⊆ closedBall(0,σ) is compact, ρ is bounded, and ρ is Lipschitz (C¹ with compact support).
 - ρ̌(x) := ρ(−x) has the same properties: C², ρ̌ ≥ 0, support ρ̌ ⊆ B(0,σ) (the ball is symmetric), and ∫ρ̌ = ∫ρ = 1 (μ is invariant under negation).
 - w := ρ * F = convolution ρ F (lsmul ℝ ℝ) volume, so w(x) = ∫ ρ(t)F(x − t) dt. w is C² (Mathlib HasCompactSupport.contDiff_convolution_left with ρ C² of compact support and F locally integrable); in particular w is C¹.
 - O := {x ∈ E : closedBall(x,σ) ⊆ W}. O is open: if closedBall(x,σ) ⊆ W, then since closedBall(x,σ) is compact and W open there is r > 0 with cthickening(r, closedBall(x,σ)) ⊆ W (Mathlib IsCompact.exists_cthickening_subset_open), and then closedBall(x',σ) ⊆ W whenever ‖x' − x‖ ≤ r. By hypothesis K ⊆ O.
 - Put M := |Du|(W). If M = ∞ there is nothing to prove. Assume M < ∞ and let m := M.toReal ≥ 0, so that ofReal m = M.

1. Duality bound for one test field (T4). Claim: for every C¹ field g : E → E with compact support, tsupport g ⊆ O and ‖g(x)‖ ≤ 1 for all x, we have ∫ w(x) div g(x) dx ≤ m.
 (a) Fubini. Let h := div g. Since g is C¹ with compact support, Dg is continuous with compact support, so h is bounded, measurable, and h = 0 off tsupport g. The function (x,t) ↦ ρ(t)F(x − t)h(x) is integrable on E × E: by Tonelli and translation invariance, ∫∫ ρ(t)|F(x − t)||h(x)| dx dt ≤ sup|h|·∫ρ·‖F‖₁ < ∞. Hence, using Fubini and the substitution x = s + t for fixed t,
   ∫ w h = ∫_t ρ(t) ∫_s F(s) h(s + t) ds dt = ∫_s F(s) (∫_t ρ(t) h(s + t) dt) ds = ∫_s F(s)·(ρ̌ * h)(s) ds,
 because ∫_t ρ(t) h(s + t) dt = ∫_t ρ(−t) h(s − t) dt = (ρ̌ * h)(s) (substitute t ↦ −t).
 (b) Divergence commutes with convolution. Let G := ρ̌ * g, the vector-valued convolution convolution ρ̌ g (lsmul ℝ ℝ) volume, so G(s) = ∫ ρ̌(t) g(s − t) dt. Since g is C¹ with compact support and ρ̌ is locally integrable, Mathlib HasCompactSupport.hasFDerivAt_convolution_right gives DG(s) = ∫ ρ̌(t) Dg(s − t) dt for every s, and G is C¹ (HasCompactSupport.contDiff_convolution_right). The trace is a continuous linear map on the finite-dimensional space E →L[ℝ] E, so it commutes with the Bochner integral (ContinuousLinearMap.integral_comp_comm). Hence div G(s) = ∫ ρ̌(t) div g(s − t) dt = (ρ̌ * h)(s) for every s.
 (c) G is admissible for W.
 - Support: support G ⊆ support ρ̌ + support g ⊆ closedBall(0,σ) + tsupport g (Mathlib support_convolution_subset). The right side is compact (a sum of compact sets), hence closed, so tsupport G ⊆ closedBall(0,σ) + tsupport g. Every y ∈ tsupport g lies in O, so y + closedBall(0,σ) = closedBall(y,σ) ⊆ W. Hence tsupport G ⊆ W, and G has compact support.
 - G is continuous with compact support, so it defines an element of C_c(E,E). It is C¹ with compact support, hence Lipschitz (ContDiff.lipschitzWith_of_hasCompactSupport), i.e. IsLipschitzTestField.
 - ‖G(s)‖ ≤ ∫ ρ̌(t)‖g(s − t)‖ dt ≤ ∫ρ̌ = 1 for every s (since ρ̌ ≥ 0). So compactlySupportedSupNorm G = sSup (range ‖G(·)‖) ≤ 1 (csSup_le; the range is nonempty).
 (d) By SimonGMT ofReal_integral_le_bvVariationOn, ofReal(∫_W u div G) ≤ M = ofReal m. Since m ≥ 0, this gives ∫_W u div G ≤ m (ENNReal.ofReal_le_ofReal_iff).
 Finally, by (a) and (b), ∫ w h = ∫ F·div G = ∫ 1_W u·div G = ∫_W u div G ≤ m.

2. Smooth duality on compact subsets of O (T5). Claim: for every compact L ⊆ O, ∫_L ‖Dw(x)‖ dx ≤ m.
 (a) A smooth cut-off. Choose r > 0 with cthickening(3r, L) ⊆ O (IsCompact.exists_cthickening_subset_open). Let ϑ be a C^∞ kernel with ϑ ≥ 0, support ϑ ⊆ B(0,r) and ∫ϑ = 1; for instance ϑ := c.normed volume for the ContDiffBump c centred at 0 with rIn = r/2 and rOut = r (Mathlib contDiff_normed, nonneg_normed, support_normed_eq, integral_normed). Put χ := ϑ * 1_{thickening(r,L)}. Then:
 - χ is C^∞ (HasCompactSupport.contDiff_convolution_left), and 0 ≤ χ ≤ 1;
 - χ = 1 on L, because for x ∈ L and ‖t‖ < r we have x − t ∈ thickening(r,L);
 - support χ ⊆ B(0,r) + thickening(r,L) ⊆ thickening(2r,L), so tsupport χ ⊆ cthickening(2r,L) ⊆ O, which is compact.
 (b) The test field. Let ∇w(x) ∈ E be the gradient, i.e. the Riesz representative of Dw(x), so that Dw(x)[v] = ⟨∇w(x), v⟩ and ‖∇w(x)‖ = ‖Dw(x)‖. Since w is C² and the Riesz map is a linear isometry, ∇w is C¹. Fix η > 0 and put
   g(x) := −χ(x)·∇w(x)/√(‖∇w(x)‖² + η²).
 g is C¹: the denominator is C¹ and ≥ η > 0, and χ is C^∞. Also tsupport g ⊆ tsupport χ ⊆ O is compact, and ‖g(x)‖ ≤ ‖∇w(x)‖/√(‖∇w(x)‖² + η²) ≤ 1. So by step 1, ∫ w div g ≤ m.
 (c) Evaluation by integration by parts. g is C¹ with compact support, hence Lipschitz, and w is C¹. By the sibling theorem Submission.bv_lipschitz_integration_by_parts (with F := w),
   ∫ w div g = −∫ Dw(x)[g(x)] dx = ∫ χ(x)·‖∇w(x)‖²/√(‖∇w(x)‖² + η²) dx,
 because Dw(x)[∇w(x)] = ‖∇w(x)‖².
 (d) Lower bound. For t ≥ 0 we have t²/√(t² + η²) ≥ t − η: if t ≤ η the left side is ≥ 0 ≥ t − η; if t > η then t²/√(t² + η²) ≥ t²/(t + η) ≥ (t² − η²)/(t + η) = t − η. Since χ ≥ 0 everywhere and χ = 1 on L, pointwise χ·‖∇w‖²/√(‖∇w‖² + η²) ≥ 1_L·(‖∇w‖ − η). All functions involved are continuous with compact support, hence integrable. Thus
   ∫_L ‖Dw‖ − η·μ(L) ≤ ∫ w div g ≤ m.
 Since η > 0 is arbitrary and μ(L) < ∞, we get ∫_L ‖Dw‖ ≤ m.

3. Passage to O and to K.
 Choose compact sets L_1 ⊆ L_2 ⊆ … (l = 1, 2, …) with ∪_l L_l = O: take L_l := {x ∈ closedBall(0,l) : infDist(x, Oᶜ) ≥ 1/l} if O ≠ E, and L_l := closedBall(0,l) if O = E. Each L_l is closed (infDist is continuous) and bounded, hence compact. It is contained in O, because infDist(x, Oᶜ) > 0 forces x ∉ Oᶜ (Oᶜ is closed). Their union is O, because every x ∈ O has infDist(x, Oᶜ) > 0 (O is open).
 For each l, ∫⁻_{L_l} ‖Dw‖ₑ = ofReal(∫_{L_l} ‖Dw‖) ≤ ofReal m = M by step 2; the integrand is continuous on a compact set, hence integrable. The measurable functions 1_{L_l}·‖Dw‖ₑ increase pointwise to 1_O·‖Dw‖ₑ. So by monotone convergence (Mathlib lintegral_iSup), ∫⁻_O ‖Dw‖ₑ = sup_l ∫⁻_{L_l} ‖Dw‖ₑ ≤ M.
 Finally K ⊆ O, so ∫⁻_K ‖Dw‖ₑ ≤ ∫⁻_O ‖Dw‖ₑ ≤ M (lintegral_mono_set; no measurability of K is needed). Here ‖Dw‖ₑ is the extended norm of fderiv ℝ w x, as in the statement. ∎

Edge cases. If W = ∅ then O = ∅ and K = ∅ (each x ∈ K satisfies x ∈ closedBall(x,σ) ⊆ W), so the left side is 0. If n = 0 then Dw = 0. Both cases are also covered by the general argument.
proof_key_steps: Set F = 1_W u ∈ L¹, w = ρ * F ∈ C², ρ̌(x) = ρ(−x), and the open set O = {x : closedBall(x,σ) ⊆ W} ⊇ K; assume |Du|(W) = ofReal m < ∞.
T4: for C¹ g with compact support in O and |g| ≤ 1, Fubini gives ∫ w div g = ∫ F (ρ̌ * div g) = ∫_W u div(ρ̌ * g), and ρ̌ * g is an admissible Lipschitz field for W; hence ∫ w div g ≤ m.

T5: for compact L ⊆ O, take g = −χ∇w/√(|∇w|²+η²) with a smooth cut-off χ (χ = 1 on L, tsupport χ ⊆ O); integrate by parts with Submission.bv_lipschitz_integration_by_parts to get ∫_L |∇w| − ηLⁿ(L) ≤ m.
Let η → 0, exhaust O by compacts (monotone convergence) and restrict to K ⊆ O: ∫⁻_K ‖Dw‖ₑ ≤ |Du|(W).

subproblems.title: L¹ mollification estimate ∫_Q |ρ*(1_W u) − u| ≤ σ|Du|(W)
subproblems.statement: For every n ∈ ℕ, every open W ⊆ ℝⁿ, every measurable Q ⊆ ℝⁿ, every u integrable on W, every σ ∈ ℝ and every continuous kernel ρ : ℝⁿ → ℝ with ρ ≥ 0, support ρ ⊆ B(0,σ) (open ball) and ∫ρ = 1, if closedBall(x,σ) ⊆ W for every x ∈ Q then ∫⁻_Q |(ρ * (1_W u))(x) − u(x)| dx ≤ ofReal(σ)·|Du|(W) in [0,∞], where ρ * (1_W u) = convolution ρ (W.indicator u) (lsmul ℝ ℝ) volume and |Du|(W) = SimonGMT bvVariationOn u W.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (n : ℕ) (W Q : Set (Rn n)) (u ρ : Rn n → ℝ) (σ : ℝ), IsOpen W → IntegrableOn u W volume → MeasurableSet Q → Continuous ρ → (∀ x, 0 ≤ ρ x) → Function.support ρ ⊆ ball 0 σ → ∫ x, ρ x = 1 → (∀ x ∈ Q, closedBall x σ ⊆ W) → ∫⁻ x in Q, ‖convolution ρ (W.indicator u) (ContinuousLinearMap.lsmul ℝ ℝ) volume x - u x‖ₑ ≤ ENNReal.ofReal σ * Chapter02.bvVariationOn u W
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: parent proof, Section T, step T7 (translation and mollification estimate: “for |z| ≤ σ: ∫_Q |u(x − z) − u(x)| dx ≤ |z||Du|(W), and ∫_Q |u_σ − u| ≤ σ|Du|(W)”). Simon's printed proof of Theorem 2.6 uses this estimate when it reduces precompactness in L¹_loc to the smooth case via Lemma 2.5 and [GT01, Thm 7.22]. Here the kernel is an arbitrary continuous kernel ρ ≥ 0 with ∫ρ = 1 and support in B(0,σ). The hypothesis Q + B̄(0,3σ) ⊆ W of the parent is relaxed to closedBall(x,σ) ⊆ W for x ∈ Q; the proof below uses the strict inequality ‖z‖ < σ, valid on the support of ρ.

Notation. E := ℝⁿ = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n), μ := volume (translation invariant). F := 1_W u = W.indicator u. For a kernel κ, κ * G := convolution κ G (lsmul ℝ ℝ) volume, i.e. (κ * G)(x) = ∫ κ(t) G(x − t) dt. Dh := fderiv ℝ h. |Du|(W) := Chapter02.bvVariationOn u W.

0. Preliminaries. W is open, hence measurable, so F ∈ L¹(E). Since ∫ρ = 1, ρ ≢ 0, so B(0,σ) ≠ ∅ and σ > 0. ρ is continuous with support in B(0,σ), hence bounded and integrable. Put M := |Du|(W). If M = ∞ the right side is ofReal(σ)·∞ = ∞ (because ofReal σ ≠ 0), and there is nothing to prove. Assume M < ∞.

1. Translation estimate. Claim: for every z ∈ E with ‖z‖ < σ,
   ∫⁻_Q |F(x − z) − F(x)| dx ≤ ofReal(‖z‖)·M.
 (a) Smooth approximants. Let m₀ := σ − ‖z‖ > 0 and τ_j := m₀/(j + 2) for j ∈ ℕ, so τ_j → 0. Let ψ_j be a C^∞ kernel with ψ_j ≥ 0, support ψ_j ⊆ B(0,τ_j) and ∫ψ_j = 1; e.g. ψ_j := c_j.normed volume for the ContDiffBump c_j centred at 0 with rIn = τ_j/2 and rOut = τ_j (Mathlib contDiff_normed, continuous_normed, nonneg_normed, support_normed_eq, integral_normed). Let w_j := ψ_j * F. It is C^∞ (HasCompactSupport.contDiff_convolution_left), in particular C², and ψ_j is C².
 (b) Gradient bound on translates of Q. For s ∈ [0,1] let Q_s := {x − s z : x ∈ Q}, a measurable set (a translate of Q). If y = x − s z with x ∈ Q, then
   closedBall(y,τ_j) ⊆ closedBall(x, s‖z‖ + τ_j) ⊆ closedBall(x,σ) ⊆ W,
 because s‖z‖ + τ_j ≤ ‖z‖ + m₀ = σ. So the sibling theorem Submission.bv_mollifier_fderiv_lintegral_le (with W, K := Q_s, u, kernel ψ_j and radius τ_j) gives
   ∫⁻_{Q_s} ‖Dw_j(y)‖ₑ dy ≤ M   for every s ∈ [0,1] and every j.
 (c) Fundamental theorem of calculus. For each x, the C¹ function s ↦ w_j(x − s z) has derivative −Dw_j(x − s z)[z]. So
   w_j(x − z) − w_j(x) = −∫_0^1 Dw_j(x − s z)[z] ds,  hence  |w_j(x − z) − w_j(x)| ≤ ‖z‖ ∫_0^1 ‖Dw_j(x − s z)‖ ds.
 The function (x,s) ↦ ‖Dw_j(x − s z)‖ is continuous. By Tonelli (lintegral_lintegral_swap) and translation invariance (∫⁻_Q f(x − s z) dx = ∫⁻_{Q_s} f(y) dy),
   ∫⁻_Q |w_j(x − z) − w_j(x)| dx ≤ ofReal‖z‖ · ∫⁻_{s∈[0,1]} ∫⁻_{Q_s} ‖Dw_j‖ₑ dy ds ≤ ofReal‖z‖ · M.
 (d) Limit j → ∞. By the sibling theorem Submission.bv_mollifier_tendsto_L1 (with F, kernels ψ_j, radii τ_j → 0), e_j := ∫⁻_E |w_j − F| → 0. By translation invariance,
   ∫⁻_Q |w_j(x − z) − F(x − z)| dx ≤ ∫⁻_E |w_j(y) − F(y)| dy = e_j,  and  ∫⁻_Q |w_j − F| ≤ e_j.
 By the pointwise triangle inequality |F(x − z) − F(x)| ≤ |F(x − z) − w_j(x − z)| + |w_j(x − z) − w_j(x)| + |w_j(x) − F(x)| and additivity of ∫⁻ for a.e.-measurable functions,
   ∫⁻_Q |F(x − z) − F(x)| dx ≤ 2e_j + ofReal‖z‖·M  for every j.
 Letting j → ∞ proves the claim.

2. Pointwise representation on Q. Let x ∈ Q. Then x ∈ closedBall(x,σ) ⊆ W, so F(x) = u(x). Since ρ is bounded with compact support and F ∈ L¹, t ↦ ρ(t)F(x − t) is integrable; and ∫ρ = 1. Therefore
   (ρ * F)(x) − u(x) = ∫ ρ(t)(F(x − t) − F(x)) dt,
 and, since ρ ≥ 0, in [0,∞]:
   ‖(ρ * F)(x) − u(x)‖ₑ ≤ ∫⁻ ofReal(ρ(t))·‖F(x − t) − F(x)‖ₑ dt.
 (Here ρ * F is exactly convolution ρ (W.indicator u) (lsmul ℝ ℝ) volume.)

3. Integration over Q and Tonelli. The function (x,t) ↦ ofReal(ρ(t))·‖F(x − t) − F(x)‖ₑ is a.e.-measurable on E × E: F is a.e.-strongly measurable and (x,t) ↦ x − t is quasi-measure-preserving. By step 2 and Tonelli (lintegral_lintegral_swap),
   ∫⁻_Q ‖ρ * F − u‖ₑ ≤ ∫⁻_t ofReal(ρ(t)) (∫⁻_Q ‖F(x − t) − F(x)‖ₑ dx) dt.
 If ρ(t) ≠ 0 then ‖t‖ < σ, so by step 1 the inner integral is ≤ ofReal(‖t‖)·M ≤ ofReal(σ)·M. If ρ(t) = 0 the integrand vanishes. Hence
   ∫⁻_Q ‖ρ * F − u‖ₑ ≤ ofReal(σ)·M·∫⁻ ofReal(ρ(t)) dt = ofReal(σ)·M,
 because ∫⁻ ofReal ρ = ofReal(∫ρ) = 1 (ofReal_integral_eq_lintegral_ofReal, ρ ≥ 0 integrable). This is the claim. ∎
proof_key_steps: Reduce to |Du|(W) = M < ∞; σ > 0 because ∫ρ = 1 and support ρ ⊆ B(0,σ).

Translation estimate for ‖z‖ < σ: mollify with C^∞ kernels ψ_j of radius τ_j ≤ σ − ‖z‖; FTC along segments + Tonelli + Submission.bv_mollifier_fderiv_lintegral_le on the translates Q − sz give ∫_Q |w_j(x−z) − w_j(x)| ≤ ‖z‖M.
Pass to F = 1_W u with Submission.bv_mollifier_tendsto_L1 and translation invariance: ∫_Q |F(x − z) − F(x)| ≤ ‖z‖M.
Write (ρ*F)(x) − u(x) = ∫ ρ(t)(F(x−t) − F(x)) dt for x ∈ Q, integrate over Q, Tonelli, and use ‖t‖ < σ on support ρ: total ≤ σM.

subproblems.title: |D|u||(O) ≤ |Du|(O) for locally integrable u
subproblems.statement: For every n ∈ ℕ, every open O ⊆ ℝⁿ and every u : ℝⁿ → ℝ locally integrable on O: bvVariationOn (x ↦ |u(x)|) O ≤ bvVariationOn u O, i.e. |D|u||(O) ≤ |Du|(O) with SimonGMT's variational definition (2.4).
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (n : ℕ) (O : Set (Rn n)) (u : Rn n → ℝ), IsOpen O → LocallyIntegrableOn u O volume → Chapter02.bvVariationOn (fun x ↦ |u x|) O ≤ Chapter02.bvVariationOn u O
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: parent proof, Section T, step T8 (|D|u|| ≤ |Du|). Simon's printed proof of Lemma 2.8 uses this inequality in the form “∫_U |D|u|| ≤ ∫_U |Du| (because |D|u|| ≤ |Du| by 2.5 and lower semicontinuity)”. The proof below mollifies, composes with a smoothed absolute value, and passes to the limit directly on each test field.

Notation. E := ℝⁿ = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n), μ := volume. For a kernel κ, κ * G := convolution κ G (lsmul ℝ ℝ) volume. Dh := fderiv ℝ h. div g := Chapter02.euclideanDivergence g. For a set A, |Dv|(A) := Chapter02.bvVariationOn v A.

0. Reduction. Let M := |Du|(O). If M = ∞ the claim is trivial. Assume M < ∞ and put m := M.toReal, so ofReal m = M. By definition |D|u||(O) = ⨆ over admissible g of ofReal(∫_O |u| div g), where g ∈ C_c(E,E) is Lipschitz (constant Λ), tsupport g ⊆ O and compactlySupportedSupNorm g ≤ 1. By iSup_le it suffices to show ∫_O |u(x)| div g(x) dx ≤ m for each such g; then ofReal(∫_O |u| div g) ≤ ofReal m = M. Fix such a g and put S := tsupport g, which is compact with S ⊆ O. For every x, ‖g(x)‖ ≤ compactlySupportedSupNorm g ≤ 1: the range of ‖g(·)‖ is bounded, so le_csSup applies.
 If S = ∅ then g = 0, div g = 0, and the integral is 0 ≤ m. Assume S ≠ ∅.

1. Neighbourhoods. Choose r > 0 with cthickening(3r, S) ⊆ O (IsCompact.exists_cthickening_subset_open). Put V := thickening(r,S) and V' := thickening(2r,S); both are open.
 - S ⊆ V ⊆ V'.
 - V' ⊆ cthickening(2r,S), which is compact (closed and bounded in E) and contained in O. Since u is locally integrable on the open set O, u is integrable on every compact subset of O (LocallyIntegrableOn.integrableOn_compact_subset), so u is integrable on V'.
 - μ(V) < ∞ because V is bounded.

2. Mollification and the gradient bound. For j ∈ ℕ let σ_j := r/(j + 2), so 0 < σ_j < r and σ_j → 0. Let ρ_j be a C^∞ kernel with ρ_j ≥ 0, support ρ_j ⊆ B(0,σ_j) and ∫ρ_j = 1; e.g. the normalized ContDiffBump at 0 with rIn = σ_j/2 and rOut = σ_j (Mathlib contDiff_normed, nonneg_normed, support_normed_eq, integral_normed). Put w_j := ρ_j * (1_{V'} u). It is C^∞ (HasCompactSupport.contDiff_convolution_left).
 Let x ∈ V and ‖y − x‖ ≤ σ_j. Then infDist(y,S) ≤ infDist(x,S) + σ_j < r + r = 2r, so y ∈ V'. Hence closedBall(x,σ_j) ⊆ V' for every x ∈ V.
 The sibling theorem Submission.bv_mollifier_fderiv_lintegral_le (with W := V', K := V, u, ρ_j, σ_j) gives
   ∫⁻_V ‖Dw_j‖ₑ ≤ |Du|(V') ≤ |Du|(O) = M.
 The middle inequality is monotonicity of bvVariationOn in the open set. Let h be admissible for V' (Lipschitz, tsupport h ⊆ V', sup norm ≤ 1). Then h is admissible for O, since V' ⊆ O. Moreover ∫_{V'} u div h = ∫_O u div h, because div h vanishes off tsupport h ⊆ V' (SimonGMT support_euclideanDivergence_subset), so both set integrals equal ∫ 1_{tsupport h} u div h. Thus every term in the supremum defining |Du|(V') also occurs in the supremum defining |Du|(O).

3. Smoothed absolute value. For η > 0 let ψ_η(t) := √(t² + η²) − η. It is C^∞ on ℝ, |ψ_η'(t)| = |t|/√(t² + η²) ≤ 1, and |t| − η ≤ ψ_η(t) ≤ |t| because |t| ≤ √(t² + η²) ≤ |t| + η. Hence |ψ_η(t) − |t|| ≤ η.
 Let η_j := 1/(j + 1) and F_j := ψ_{η_j} ∘ w_j. Then F_j is C^∞ (in particular C¹) with DF_j(x) = ψ_{η_j}'(w_j(x))·Dw_j(x).

4. Integration by parts and the uniform bound. g is Lipschitz with compact support and F_j is C¹. By the sibling theorem Submission.bv_lipschitz_integration_by_parts,
   ∫ F_j div g = −∫ ψ_{η_j}'(w_j(x))·Dw_j(x)[g(x)] dx.
 Pointwise |ψ'(w_j(x)) Dw_j(x)[g(x)]| ≤ ‖Dw_j(x)‖·‖g(x)‖ ≤ ‖Dw_j(x)‖·1_S(x), because |ψ'| ≤ 1, ‖g‖ ≤ 1, and g = 0 off S. The functions involved are continuous with compact support, hence integrable. Therefore
   ∫ F_j div g ≤ ∫_S ‖Dw_j‖ = (∫⁻_S ‖Dw_j‖ₑ).toReal ≤ (∫⁻_V ‖Dw_j‖ₑ).toReal ≤ m,
 using S ⊆ V, step 2, and the finiteness of these integrals.

5. Limit j → ∞.
 - div g = 0 off S ⊆ V, and |div g| ≤ nΛ everywhere (SimonGMT norm_euclideanDivergence_le_of_lipschitz). So ∫ F_j div g = ∫_V F_j div g.
 - On V we have 1_{V'}u = u, so |F_j − |u|| ≤ |ψ_{η_j}(w_j) − |w_j|| + ||w_j| − |u|| ≤ η_j + |w_j − 1_{V'}u|.
 - Hence |∫_V F_j div g − ∫_V |u| div g| ≤ nΛ(η_j μ(V) + ∫ |w_j − 1_{V'}u|) → 0. Here ∫ |w_j − 1_{V'}u| → 0 by the sibling theorem Submission.bv_mollifier_tendsto_L1 (with F := 1_{V'}u ∈ L¹, kernels ρ_j, radii σ_j → 0); the lower integral there is finite and converges to 0, so its toReal does too. Also μ(V) < ∞ and η_j → 0. The function |u| div g is integrable on V because u ∈ L¹(V) and div g is bounded.
 Since ∫_V F_j div g ≤ m for all j, the limit gives ∫_V |u| div g ≤ m. Finally ∫_O |u| div g = ∫_V |u| div g, because |u| div g vanishes on O ∖ V ⊆ E ∖ S. So ∫_O |u| div g ≤ m, which completes the reduction of step 0. ∎

Edge cases. If O = ∅, every admissible g has empty tsupport, so both sides are 0. If n = 0, every div g vanishes. Both cases are also covered by the argument above.
proof_key_steps: Reduce to a single admissible Lipschitz field g for O with S = tsupport g ≠ ∅, assuming |Du|(O) = ofReal m < ∞.

Thicken S: V = thickening(r,S), V' = thickening(2r,S) ⊂⊂ O; mollify w_j = ρ_j * (1_{V'}u) and bound ∫_V ‖Dw_j‖ ≤ |Du|(V') ≤ |Du|(O) via Submission.bv_mollifier_fderiv_lintegral_le and monotonicity of bvVariationOn.
With ψ_η(t) = √(t²+η²) − η, integrate by parts (Submission.bv_lipschitz_integration_by_parts): ∫ ψ_η(w_j) div g ≤ ∫_S ‖Dw_j‖ ≤ m.
Let j → ∞ with η_j → 0: ψ_{η_j}(w_j) → |u| in L¹(V) (Submission.bv_mollifier_tendsto_L1), so ∫_O |u| div g = ∫_V |u| div g ≤ m.

subproblems.title: Simon 2.6: compactness theorem for BV_loc (frozen BVCompactness)
subproblems.statement: (Simon Ch. 2, Theorem 2.6, frozen contract BVCompactness.) For every n, every U ⊆ ℝⁿ and every sequence u_k (k ∈ ℕ) with each u_k locally BV on U (SimonGMT IsLocallyBV U (u k)) such that for every open W ⊂⊂ U (IsRelativelyCompactIn W U: closure W compact and ⊆ U) the quantity sup_k ∫⁻_W (‖u_k(x)‖ₑ + bvVariationOn (u k) W) dx is finite (the x-independent constant |Du_k|(W) = bvVariationOn (u k) W sits inside the integrand), there are a strictly increasing ψ : ℕ → ℕ and v : ℝⁿ → ℝ such that v is locally BV on U, u_{ψ(k)} → v in L¹_loc(U) (TendstoLocallyInL1On), and bvVariationOn v W ≤ liminf_k bvVariationOn (u (ψ k)) W for every open W ⊂⊂ U.
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: Simon, Introduction to GMT, Ch. 2, Theorem 2.6 (p. 50). Printed proof (cleaned transcription, as in the parent): “By virtue of the previous lemma, in order to prove u_{k'} → u in L¹_loc(U) for some subsequence, it is enough to prove that the sets {u ∈ C¹(U) : ∫_W (|u| + |Du|) dLⁿ ≤ c(W)}, W ⊂⊂ U (for given constants c(W) < ∞), are precompact in L¹_loc(U). For the simple proof of this (involving mollification and Arzela's theorem) see [GT01, Thm 7.22]. Finally the fact that ∫_W|Du| ≤ liminf ∫_W |Du_{k'}| is a direct consequence of the definition of |Du|, |Du_{k'}|.”
Erratum/reading (GMT/Ch02/README.md): the sets W ⊂⊂ U are open; lower semicontinuity fails for non-open W, and 2.4 characterizes |Du|(W) only for open W.
Frozen hypothesis: ⨆ k, (∫⁻ x in W, ‖u k x‖ₑ + Chapter02.bvVariationOn (u k) W) < ⊤ for every open W ⊂⊂ U. The whole sum is the integrand; step A0 converts this into the printed unweighted bound.
The complete argument below is Section A of the parent proof. The mollification estimate T7 is supplied by the sibling theorem Submission.bv_mollifier_sub_lintegral_le.

Notation. E := ℝⁿ = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n), μ := volume. |Dv|(W) := Chapter02.bvVariationOn v W. For a kernel κ, κ * G := convolution κ G (lsmul ℝ ℝ) volume, so (κ * G)(x) = ∫ κ(t)G(x − t) dt = ∫ κ(x − s)G(s) ds. W ⊂⊂ U means Chapter02.IsRelativelyCompactIn W U. Fix n, U and u satisfying the hypotheses. By IsLocallyBV U (u 0), U is open, and each u_k is locally integrable on U.

A0. Unweighted uniform bound. For every open W ⊂⊂ U, put S_W := ⨆_k ∫⁻_W (‖u_k(x)‖ₑ + |Du_k|(W)) dx < ∞. Claim: C_W := ⨆_k (∫⁻_W ‖u_k‖ₑ + |Du_k|(W)) is finite.
 (a) W = ∅. The integral over ∅ is 0, because volume.restrict ∅ = 0. Also |Du_k|(∅) = 0: every term of the supremum defining bvVariationOn (u k) ∅ is ofReal(∫_∅ …) = ofReal 0 = 0, and a supremum of zeros (or an empty one) is 0. Hence C_∅ = 0.
 (b) W ≠ ∅. Then 0 < μ(W) < ∞: W is nonempty and open and μ is an additive Haar measure (IsOpen.measure_pos; for n = 0 the space is a point of measure 1), and μ(W) ≤ μ(closure W) < ∞ because closure W is compact (IsCompact.measure_lt_top). Fix k. The function x ↦ |Du_k|(W) is constant, hence measurable, so by lintegral_add_right and setLIntegral_const
   ∫⁻_W (‖u_k(x)‖ₑ + |Du_k|(W)) dx = ∫⁻_W ‖u_k‖ₑ + |Du_k|(W)·μ(W) ≤ S_W.
 Hence ∫⁻_W ‖u_k‖ₑ ≤ S_W and |Du_k|(W)·μ(W) ≤ S_W, so |Du_k|(W) ≤ S_W/μ(W) (ENNReal.le_div_iff_mul_le, using μ(W) ≠ 0 and μ(W) ≠ ∞). Thus C_W ≤ S_W + S_W/μ(W) < ∞ (ENNReal.div_lt_top).
 (c) Consequences. Put c_W := C_W.toReal ≥ 0, so ofReal c_W = C_W. Then for every k: ∫⁻_W ‖u_k‖ₑ ≤ ofReal c_W, so u_k ∈ L¹(W) with ∫_W |u_k| ≤ c_W (u_k is locally integrable on U and closure W is a compact subset of U). Also |Du_k|(W) ≤ ofReal c_W < ∞, so (|Du_k|(W)).toReal ≤ c_W. This is the printed hypothesis sup_k (∫_W|u_k| + |Du_k|(W)) < ∞.

A1. Total boundedness on compact sets. Fix a compact Q ⊆ U; if Q = ∅ there is nothing to prove. Choose δ > 0 with cthickening(2δ, Q) ⊆ U (IsCompact.exists_cthickening_subset_open). Let W := thickening(δ, Q), an open set with Q ⊆ W. Its closure is contained in cthickening(δ, Q), which is compact and ⊆ U, so W ⊂⊂ U. Let c_W be the constant of A0 for this W.
 Fix ε > 0. Choose σ ∈ (0, δ) with σ·c_W < ε/4. Let ρ be a C^∞ kernel with ρ ≥ 0, support ρ ⊆ B(0,σ) and ∫ρ = 1; e.g. the normalized ContDiffBump at 0 with rIn = σ/2 and rOut = σ (Mathlib contDiff_normed, continuous_normed, nonneg_normed, support_normed_eq, integral_normed). For x ∈ Q, closedBall(x,σ) ⊆ thickening(δ,Q) = W because σ < δ. Put v_k := ρ * (1_W u_k).
 (i) Mollification error. Q is compact, hence measurable. By the sibling theorem Submission.bv_mollifier_sub_lintegral_le (with W, Q, u_k, ρ, σ; u_k ∈ L¹(W) by A0(c)),
   ∫⁻_Q ‖v_k − u_k‖ₑ ≤ ofReal(σ)·|Du_k|(W) ≤ ofReal(σ c_W) for every k.
 (ii) Uniform bounds (T1). ρ is C¹ with compact support, hence bounded by some A_ρ and Λ_ρ-Lipschitz. Writing v_k(x) = ∫ ρ(x − s)(1_W u_k)(s) ds, for all x, y and k:
   |v_k(x)| ≤ A_ρ ∫_W |u_k| ≤ B := A_ρ c_W,
   |v_k(x) − v_k(y)| ≤ ∫ |ρ(x − s) − ρ(y − s)||1_W u_k(s)| ds ≤ Λ ‖x − y‖ with Λ := Λ_ρ c_W.
 (iii) Elementary Arzelà–Ascoli. Let η := ε/(4(μ(Q).toReal + 1)). Since Q is compact, pick a finite set {q_1, …, q_p} ⊆ Q such that every x ∈ Q satisfies ‖x − q_i‖ < η/(3Λ + 3) for some i. Let Γ be the finite set (η/3)ℤ ∩ [−B − η, B + η]. For each k let a(k) ∈ Γ^p be obtained by rounding each value v_k(q_i) ∈ [−B, B] to a nearest point of Γ, so that |v_k(q_i) − a(k)_i| ≤ η/6 for all i (the grid spacing is η/3). Γ^p is finite, so the indices k fall into finitely many classes {k : a(k) = a}; pick one representative k_s in each nonempty class (s = 1, …, r).
 If a(k) = a(k'), then |v_k(q_i) − v_{k'}(q_i)| ≤ η/6 + η/6 = η/3 for every i. For x ∈ Q, choosing q_i with ‖x − q_i‖ < η/(3Λ + 3),
   |v_k(x) − v_{k'}(x)| ≤ |v_k(x) − v_k(q_i)| + |v_k(q_i) − v_{k'}(q_i)| + |v_{k'}(q_i) − v_{k'}(x)| ≤ 2Λη/(3Λ + 3) + η/3 < 2η/3 + η/3 = η,
 because 2Λ/(3Λ + 3) < 2/3.
 Hence ∫_Q |v_k − v_{k_s}| ≤ η μ(Q) < ε/4 for the representative k_s of the class of k.
 (iv) Conclusion. For every k there is s with
   ∫⁻_Q ‖u_k − u_{k_s}‖ₑ ≤ ∫⁻_Q ‖u_k − v_k‖ₑ + ∫⁻_Q ‖v_k − v_{k_s}‖ₑ + ∫⁻_Q ‖v_{k_s} − u_{k_s}‖ₑ < ofReal(3ε/4).
 So the set {[u_k|_Q] : k ∈ ℕ} is totally bounded in the complete metric space L¹(Q) := Lp ℝ 1 (volume.restrict Q). Each u_k is integrable on Q because Q is a compact subset of U.

A2. Diagonal extraction and the limit v.
 (a) Exhaustion. If U = ∅, take ψ := id and v := 0; all claims below are then trivial (every compact K ⊆ U and every W ⊂⊂ U is empty, IsLocallyBV ∅ 0 holds by SimonGMT isLocallyBV_zero, and bvVariationOn _ ∅ = 0). Otherwise let Q_j := {x ∈ closedBall(0,j) : infDist(x, Uᶜ) ≥ 1/j} if U ≠ E, and Q_j := closedBall(0,j) if U = E (j ≥ 1). Each Q_j is compact, Q_j ⊆ U, Q_j ⊆ interior Q_{j+1}, and ∪_j Q_j = U. Every compact K ⊆ U is covered by the increasing open sets interior Q_{j+1}, hence K ⊆ Q_j for some j.
 (b) Subsequences. In a complete metric space the closure of a totally bounded set is compact (TotallyBounded.isCompact_closure / isCompact_of_totallyBounded_isClosed), and every sequence in a compact metric set has a convergent subsequence (IsCompact.tendsto_subseq). Apply this successively. Choose ψ_1 strictly increasing such that ([u_{ψ_1(k)}|_{Q_1}]) converges in L¹(Q_1). Given ψ_j, choose φ_{j+1} strictly increasing such that ([u_{ψ_j(φ_{j+1}(k))}|_{Q_{j+1}}]) converges in L¹(Q_{j+1}), and set ψ_{j+1} := ψ_j ∘ φ_{j+1}. By A1 the range of each sequence lies in a totally bounded set.
 Let ψ(k) := ψ_k(k). Then ψ is strictly increasing: ψ(k+1) = ψ_k(φ_{k+1}(k+1)) ≥ ψ_k(k+1) > ψ_k(k). For each j, (ψ(k))_{k ≥ j} is a subsequence of (ψ_j(k))_k. Hence ([u_{ψ(k)}|_{Q_j}]) converges in L¹(Q_j) for every j.
 (c) The limit. Let v_j be a representative (an a.e.-strongly measurable function) of the L¹(Q_j)-limit, so ∫⁻_{Q_j} ‖u_{ψ(k)} − v_j‖ₑ → 0. For i < j, L¹-limits are a.e. unique, so v_j = v_i a.e. on Q_i. Define v := v_1 on Q_1, v := v_j on Q_j ∖ Q_{j−1} for j ≥ 2, and v := 0 off U. Then v = v_j a.e. on Q_j for every j, so ∫⁻_{Q_j} ‖u_{ψ(k)} − v‖ₑ → 0 for every j.
 (d) Local L¹ convergence and local integrability. If K ⊆ U is compact, then K ⊆ Q_j for some j, so ∫⁻_K ‖u_{ψ(k)} − v‖ₑ ≤ ∫⁻_{Q_j} ‖u_{ψ(k)} − v‖ₑ → 0. This is Chapter02.TendstoLocallyInL1On (fun k ↦ u (ψ k)) v U atTop. Moreover v is integrable on each Q_j (it is the a.e.-limit representative of an L¹(Q_j) element). Every point of the open set U has a compact neighbourhood contained in some Q_j, so LocallyIntegrableOn v U volume.

A3. Lower semicontinuity. Let W be open with W ⊂⊂ U. Apply SimonGMT Chapter02.bvVariationOn_le_liminf_of_locallyL1 with l = atTop, hu: LocallyIntegrableOn v U (A2(d)), hv: ∀ᶠ k, LocallyIntegrableOn (u (ψ k)) U (from IsLocallyBV), hL1 from A2(d), and hW: W ⊂⊂ U. It gives bvVariationOn v W ≤ liminf_k bvVariationOn (u (ψ k)) W. (For each admissible g, ∫_W v div g = lim_k ∫_W u_{ψ(k)} div g, because u_{ψ(k)} → v in L¹(closure W) and div g is bounded; and each term is ≤ |Du_{ψ(k)}|(W).)

A4. v is locally BV. Let W be open with W ⊂⊂ U and let c_W ≥ 0 be the constant of A0. Claim: for every k and every IsC1TestField g with tsupport g ⊆ W, ∫_W u_k div g ≤ c_W·s, where s := compactlySupportedSupNorm g ≥ 0.
 - If s = 0 then g ≡ 0 (every ‖g(x)‖ ≤ s), so div g ≡ 0 and ∫_W u_k div g = 0 = c_W·s.
 - If s > 0, put h := s⁻¹g. A compactly supported C¹ field is Lipschitz (SimonGMT IsC1TestField.isLipschitzTestField), and scaling preserves this; tsupport h = tsupport g ⊆ W, and compactlySupportedSupNorm h = s⁻¹·s = 1 ≤ 1. Since g is differentiable, Dh = s⁻¹Dg, so div h = s⁻¹ div g and ∫_W u_k div h = s⁻¹∫_W u_k div g. By SimonGMT ofReal_integral_le_bvVariationOn, ofReal(s⁻¹∫_W u_k div g) ≤ |Du_k|(W) ≤ ofReal c_W (A0(c)). Hence s⁻¹∫_W u_k div g ≤ c_W, i.e. ∫_W u_k div g ≤ c_W·s.
 So the hypothesis hbound of SimonGMT Chapter02.isLocallyBV_of_locallyL1_of_uniform_bound holds with c := c_W for all indices, in particular eventually along atTop for the subsequence u_{ψ(k)}. Together with U open, LocallyIntegrableOn v U, LocallyIntegrableOn (u (ψ k)) U, and TendstoLocallyInL1On (fun k ↦ u (ψ k)) v U atTop (A2), that lemma gives IsLocallyBV U v.

A5. Conclusion. ψ is strictly increasing (A2(b)), IsLocallyBV U v (A4), TendstoLocallyInL1On (fun k ↦ u (ψ k)) v U atTop (A2(d)), and the liminf inequality holds for every open W ⊂⊂ U (A3). This is exactly BVCompactness. ∎
proof_key_steps: A0: split the frozen integrand (constant |Du_k|(W) inside) and divide by 0 < Lⁿ(W) < ∞ (W = ∅ separately) to get c_W ≥ sup_k(∫_W|u_k| + |Du_k|(W)).

A1: for compact Q ⊆ U, W = thickening(δ,Q) ⊂⊂ U; Submission.bv_mollifier_sub_lintegral_le gives ∫_Q|ρ*(1_W u_k) − u_k| ≤ σ c_W uniformly in k; mollifications are uniformly bounded and equi-Lipschitz; elementary Arzelà–Ascoli ⇒ {u_k|_Q} totally bounded in L¹(Q).

A2: compact exhaustion Q_j of U, compactness of closures of totally bounded sets in the complete spaces L¹(Q_j), diagonal subsequence ψ, glued limit v; TendstoLocallyInL1On and LocallyIntegrableOn v U.
A3: lower semicontinuity from SimonGMT bvVariationOn_le_liminf_of_locallyL1.
A4: rescale C¹ test fields by their sup norm to get ∫_W u_k div g ≤ c_W sup|g|, then SimonGMT isLocallyBV_of_locallyL1_of_uniform_bound gives IsLocallyBV U v.

subproblems.title: Simon 2.7: Poincaré inequality for BV on convex sets (frozen BVPoincare)
subproblems.statement: (Simon Ch. 2, Lemma 2.7, frozen contract BVPoincare.) For all n ∈ ℕ and θ, δ ∈ (0,1) there is C ≥ 0 such that for every bounded open convex U ⊆ ℝⁿ, R > 0, ξ ∈ U with closedBall(ξ,δR) ⊆ U ⊆ closedBall(ξ,R), every u with IsBVOn U u (U open, u integrable on U, bvVariationOn u U < ∞) and every β ∈ ℝ with ofReal θ·Lⁿ(U) ≤ min(Lⁿ{x ∈ U : β ≤ u(x)}, Lⁿ{x ∈ U : u(x) ≤ β}): ∫⁻_U ‖u(x) − β‖ₑ dx ≤ ofReal(C·R)·bvVariationOn u U.
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: Simon, Introduction to GMT, Ch. 2, Lemma 2.7 (p. 51). Printed proof (cleaned transcription, as in the parent): “By rescaling x ↦ R⁻¹(x − ξ) we can assume R = 1, ξ = 0. Let β, θ be as in 2.7(*) and choose convex W ⊂⊂ U such that (*) ∫_W |u − β| ≥ ½∫_U |u − β| and such that 2.7(*) holds with W in place of U and θ/2 in place of θ (e.g. W = {x ∈ U : dist(x, ∂U) > σ} with σ small). Letting u_σ denote the mollified functions, for sufficiently small σ we have 2.7(*) with u_σ in place of u, θ/4 in place of θ and W in place of U. Hence by the usual Poincaré inequality for smooth functions we have, with suitable β(σ) → β, ∫_W |u_σ − β(σ)| ≤ c ∫_W |Du_σ|, c = c(n,θ,δ), for all sufficiently small σ. The required inequality follows by letting σ ↓ 0 and using (*) and 2.5.”
Reading (GMT/Ch02/README.md): u ∈ BV(U) includes u ∈ L¹(U) (contract IsBVOn). The complete argument below is Section B of the parent proof. It works with the mean ū instead of β(σ), proves the smooth convex Poincaré inequality (B1), and then passes from ū to β (B5). The mollifier gradient bound (T6) and the L¹ convergence (T2) are the sibling theorems Submission.bv_mollifier_fderiv_lintegral_le and Submission.bv_mollifier_tendsto_L1.

Notation. E := ℝⁿ = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n), μ := volume = Lⁿ. |Du|(U) := Chapter02.bvVariationOn u U. For a kernel κ, κ * G := convolution κ G (lsmul ℝ ℝ) volume. Dw := fderiv ℝ w.

Choice of constant. Given n and θ, δ ∈ (0,1), put C := 2^{n+1}(1 + θ⁻¹) ≥ 0; it does not depend on δ. Let U, R, ξ, u, β satisfy the hypotheses. Then u ∈ L¹(U) and M := |Du|(U) < ∞ (IsBVOn), and we write m := M.toReal, so ofReal m = M. Also 0 < μ(U) < ∞, because U is open and nonempty (ξ ∈ U) and U ⊆ closedBall(ξ,R). Finally diam U ≤ 2R. Put ū := μ(U)⁻¹∫_U u.

Case n = 0. E is a single point of measure 1, so U = {ξ} = E and μ(U) = 1. Each of the sets {x ∈ U : β ≤ u(x)} and {x ∈ U : u(x) ≤ β} is either ∅ (measure 0) or {ξ} (measure 1). The hypothesis ofReal θ·1 ≤ min(…) with θ > 0 forces both to be {ξ}, so β ≤ u(ξ) ≤ β, i.e. u(ξ) = β. Then ∫⁻_U ‖u − β‖ₑ = 0 ≤ ofReal(C·R)·M. From now on n ≥ 1.

B1. Smooth Poincaré inequality on convex sets. Let O ⊆ E be open, convex and bounded with μ(O) > 0, and let w ∈ C¹(E). Put D := diam O and w̄_O := μ(O)⁻¹∫_O w (w is bounded on the bounded set O, hence integrable there). Claim:
   ∫_O |w − w̄_O| ≤ 2ⁿ D ∫_O ‖Dw‖.
 Proof.
 (a) For x, y ∈ O the segment [x,y] lies in O. By the fundamental theorem of calculus,
   |w(y) − w(x)| ≤ ‖y − x‖ ∫_0^1 ‖Dw(x + t(y − x))‖ dt ≤ D ∫_0^1 f((1 − t)x + ty) dt,
 where f := 1_O‖Dw‖ ≥ 0 (on the segment, f = ‖Dw‖).
 (b) Integrate over O × O and use Tonelli; the integrand is measurable since it is continuous times indicators of open sets:
   ∫_O∫_O |w(x) − w(y)| dy dx ≤ D ∫_0^1 ∫_O∫_O f((1 − t)x + ty) dy dx dt.
 (c) For t ∈ [½, 1] and fixed x ∈ O, the affine map y ↦ (1 − t)x + ty has Jacobian tⁿ ≥ 2^{−n} (Lebesgue measure scales by |t|ⁿ under dilation and is translation invariant). So ∫_O f((1 − t)x + ty) dy ≤ t^{−n}∫ f ≤ 2ⁿ∫_O ‖Dw‖. For t ∈ [0, ½), swap the order of integration and fix y ∈ O; the map x ↦ (1 − t)x + ty has Jacobian (1 − t)ⁿ ≥ 2^{−n}, so the inner integral is again ≤ 2ⁿ∫_O ‖Dw‖. Hence for every t ∈ [0,1], ∫_O∫_O f((1 − t)x + ty) dy dx ≤ 2ⁿ μ(O) ∫_O ‖Dw‖, and
   ∫_O∫_O |w(x) − w(y)| dy dx ≤ 2ⁿ D μ(O) ∫_O ‖Dw‖.
 (d) For x ∈ O, |w(x) − w̄_O| = |μ(O)⁻¹∫_O (w(x) − w(y)) dy| ≤ μ(O)⁻¹∫_O |w(x) − w(y)| dy. Integrating over x ∈ O gives the claim.

B2. Inner parallel sets. d(x) := infDist(x, Uᶜ). Since n ≥ 1 and U is bounded, Uᶜ ≠ ∅. Then d is 1-Lipschitz, d = 0 off U, and d > 0 on U (U is open). For σ > 0 put U_σ := {x : d(x) > σ}. Then:
 - U_σ is open (d is continuous), U_σ ⊆ U, and diam U_σ ≤ diam U ≤ 2R.
 - U_σ is convex. Let x, y ∈ U_σ and t ∈ [0,1], and pick s with σ < s < min(d(x), d(y)). Then ball(x,s) ⊆ U and ball(y,s) ⊆ U, because points at distance < d(x) from x lie in U. For ‖a‖ < s, (1 − t)x + ty + a = (1 − t)(x + a) + t(y + a) ∈ U by convexity of U. So ball((1 − t)x + ty, s) ⊆ U, hence d((1 − t)x + ty) ≥ s > σ.
 - If x ∈ U_σ then closedBall(x,σ) ⊆ U: any p ∉ U has ‖x − p‖ ≥ d(x) > σ.
 - U_σ increases as σ decreases, and ∪_{σ>0} U_σ = U.
 - Since d(ξ) > 0, for σ < d(ξ) we have ξ ∈ U_σ, so μ(U_σ) > 0 (nonempty open set).

B3. Approximation. Let σ_j := d(ξ)/(j + 2), so 0 < σ_j < d(ξ) and σ_j ↓ 0. Let ρ_j be a C^∞ kernel with ρ_j ≥ 0, support ρ_j ⊆ B(0,σ_j) and ∫ρ_j = 1; e.g. the normalized ContDiffBump at 0 with rIn = σ_j/2 and rOut = σ_j (Mathlib contDiff_normed, continuous_normed, nonneg_normed, support_normed_eq, integral_normed). Put w_j := ρ_j * (1_U u). It is C^∞ (HasCompactSupport.contDiff_convolution_left), in particular C¹; and ρ_j is C².
 By B2, closedBall(x,σ_j) ⊆ U for every x ∈ U_{σ_j}. So the sibling theorem Submission.bv_mollifier_fderiv_lintegral_le (with W := U, K := U_{σ_j}, u, ρ_j, σ_j) gives ∫⁻_{U_{σ_j}} ‖Dw_j‖ₑ ≤ M; hence ∫_{U_{σ_j}} ‖Dw_j‖ ≤ m.
 By B1 with O := U_{σ_j} (open, convex, bounded, positive measure, diameter ≤ 2R),
   ∫_{U_{σ_j}} |w_j − c_j| ≤ 2ⁿ·2R·m = 2^{n+1}R m,  where c_j := μ(U_{σ_j})⁻¹∫_{U_{σ_j}} w_j.

B4. Limit j → ∞.
 - By the sibling theorem Submission.bv_mollifier_tendsto_L1 (with F := 1_U u ∈ L¹, kernels ρ_j, radii σ_j → 0), e_j := ∫|w_j − 1_U u| → 0.
 - The sets U_{σ_j} increase with union U, so μ(U_{σ_j}) → μ(U) (continuity from below). Since μ(U) < ∞, μ(U ∖ U_{σ_j}) → 0, and ∫_{U∖U_{σ_j}} |g| → 0 for every g ∈ L¹(U) (dominated convergence).
 - On U_{σ_j} ⊆ U we have 1_U u = u. Hence |∫_{U_{σ_j}} w_j − ∫_U u| ≤ e_j + ∫_{U∖U_{σ_j}}|u| → 0, and therefore c_j → ū.
 - Moreover,
   |∫_{U_{σ_j}} |w_j − c_j| − ∫_U |u − ū|| ≤ ∫_{U_{σ_j}} |w_j − u| + |c_j − ū| μ(U) + ∫_{U∖U_{σ_j}} |u − ū| ≤ e_j + |c_j − ū| μ(U) + ∫_{U∖U_{σ_j}} |u − ū| → 0.
 Therefore I := ∫_U |u − ū| ≤ 2^{n+1} R m.

B5. From the mean to β. Since u is a.e.-strongly measurable on the measurable set U, the sets S₊ := {x ∈ U : β ≤ u(x)} and S₋ := {x ∈ U : u(x) ≤ β} are null-measurable for μ. So their measures (as written in the contract, i.e. outer measures) may be used in Markov-type lower bounds (Mathlib mul_meas_ge_le_lintegral₀). By hypothesis ofReal θ·μ(U) ≤ μ(S₊) and ofReal θ·μ(U) ≤ μ(S₋).
 - If β ≥ ū, then |u − ū| ≥ β − ū ≥ 0 on S₊, so (β − ū)·θμ(U) ≤ (β − ū)μ(S₊) ≤ I.
 - If β < ū, then |u − ū| ≥ ū − β on S₋, so (ū − β)·θμ(U) ≤ I.
 In both cases μ(U)|β − ū| ≤ θ⁻¹I. Hence
   ∫_U |u − β| ≤ ∫_U |u − ū| + μ(U)|ū − β| ≤ (1 + θ⁻¹)I ≤ (1 + θ⁻¹)2^{n+1}R m = C·R·m.
 Since u is integrable on U, ∫⁻_U ‖u − β‖ₑ = ofReal(∫_U |u − β|) ≤ ofReal(C·R·m) = ofReal(C·R)·ofReal(m) = ofReal(C·R)·bvVariationOn u U. Here C·R ≥ 0 and m ≥ 0, and ofReal m = M because M < ∞.
 This proves BVPoincare with C = 2^{n+1}(1 + θ⁻¹). ∎
proof_key_steps: Constant C = 2^{n+1}(1 + 1/θ); dispose of n = 0 (U is a point and the β-hypothesis forces u = β).
B1: smooth L¹ Poincaré on convex O: ∫_O|w − w̄_O| ≤ 2ⁿ diam(O) ∫_O|Dw| (segment FTC, split t ≤ ½ / t ≥ ½, dilation Jacobians ≥ 2^{−n}).
B2–B3: convex inner parallel sets U_σ = {dist(·,Uᶜ) > σ}; mollify w_j = ρ_j * (1_U u) and use Submission.bv_mollifier_fderiv_lintegral_le on U_{σ_j} to get ∫_{U_{σ_j}}|w_j − c_j| ≤ 2^{n+1}R|Du|(U).
B4: Submission.bv_mollifier_tendsto_L1 and U_{σ_j} ↑ U give c_j → ū and ∫_U|u − ū| ≤ 2^{n+1}R|Du|(U).
B5: Markov on the null-measurable sets {u ≥ β}, {u ≤ β} gives θLⁿ(U)|β − ū| ≤ ∫_U|u − ū|, hence ∫_U|u − β| ≤ (1 + 1/θ)2^{n+1}R|Du|(U).

subproblems.title: Simon 2.8: BV extension estimate on convex sets (frozen BVExtensionEstimate)
subproblems.statement: (Simon Ch. 2, Lemma 2.8, frozen contract BVExtensionEstimate.) For all n ∈ ℕ and δ ∈ (0,1) there is C ≥ 0 such that for every bounded open convex U ⊆ ℝⁿ, R > 0, ξ ∈ U with closedBall(ξ,δR) ⊆ U ⊆ closedBall(ξ,R), and every u with IsBVOn univ u (u ∈ L¹(ℝⁿ), bvVariationOn u univ < ∞) and u = 0 a.e. off closure U: bvVariationOn u (closure U)ᶜ = 0 and bvVariationOn u univ ≤ ofReal C·(bvVariationOn u U + ofReal R⁻¹·∫⁻_U ‖u‖ₑ).
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: Simon, Introduction to GMT, Ch. 2, Lemma 2.8 (pp. 51–53). Printed proof (cleaned transcription, as in the parent): “Assume R = 1, ξ = 0. Let d(x) = dist(x, ∂U). Since U is convex, U_σ = {x : dist(x,∂U) > σ} is convex for each σ ≥ 0 […] and 0 < d(x) < d(y) ⇒ (y − x)·Dd(x) ≥ 0 for all x ∈ U at which d is differentiable. Since B_δ(0) ⊆ U and |Dd(x)| = 1 at points of differentiability in U, taking y = −δDd(x) gives (1) x·Dd(x) ≤ −δ for a.e. x ∈ U with d(x) < dist(B_δ(0), ∂U). Let γ : ℝ → [0,1] be increasing, C¹, γ(t) = 0 for t ≤ σ/2, γ(t) = 1 for t ≥ σ, and (2) φ = γ∘d. Then (3) δ|Dφ(x)| ≤ −x·Dφ(x). By definition of |Dw|, (4) ∫|D(φu)| ≤ ∫|Dφ||u| + ∫ φ|Du|, and by (3) (5) δ∫|Dφ||u| ≤ −∫ x·Dφ |u| = ∫ |u| div(xφ) … ≤ ∫_U |D|u|| + n∫|u| ≤ ∫_U |Du| + n∫|u| (because |D|u|| ≤ |Du| by 2.5 and lower semicontinuity). Finally ∫_{ℝⁿ}|Du| ≤ liminf ∫|D(φu)| since φu → u in L¹, and 2.8 follows from (4), (5).”
Readings (GMT/Ch02/README.md): spt u ⊂ Ū means u = 0 a.e. off Ū, and ∫_{ℝⁿ}|Du| = ∫_Ū|Du| is encoded as |Du|(ℝⁿ∖Ū) = 0. As in the parent, the printed cut-off argument is kept, but the final limit is taken directly on test fields (no product lower semicontinuity). The cut-offs are Lipschitz, built from a piecewise-linear γ and level sets of d chosen to be null. The complete argument below is Section C of the parent proof. The inequality |D|u||(U) ≤ |Du|(U) is the sibling theorem Submission.bv_abs_variation_le.

Notation. E := ℝⁿ = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n), μ := volume. |Dv|(A) := Chapter02.bvVariationOn v A. div g := Chapter02.euclideanDivergence g = trace Dg, with Dg := fderiv ℝ g (0 at points of non-differentiability). A field g ∈ C_c(E,E) is admissible for an open set A if it is Lipschitz (IsLipschitzTestField), tsupport g ⊆ A and compactlySupportedSupNorm g ≤ 1; then ‖g(x)‖ ≤ 1 for all x (le_csSup on the bounded range). By SimonGMT ofReal_integral_le_bvVariationOn, ofReal(∫_A v div g) ≤ |Dv|(A) for every admissible g. Recall also: div g is Borel (measurable_euclideanDivergence), |div g| ≤ nΛ for a Λ-Lipschitz g (norm_euclideanDivergence_le_of_lipschitz), div g = 0 off tsupport g (support_euclideanDivergence_subset), and Lipschitz maps on E are differentiable a.e. (Rademacher, LipschitzWith.ae_differentiableAt).

Choice of constant. Given n and δ ∈ (0,1), put C := max(1 + δ⁻¹, nδ⁻¹) ≥ 1 > 0. Let U, R, ξ, u satisfy the hypotheses: u ∈ L¹(E), |Du|(E) < ∞, and u = 0 a.e. on E ∖ closure U.

C0. |Du|(E ∖ closure U) = 0. The set A := (closure U)ᶜ is open and measurable. For g admissible for A: since u = 0 μ-a.e. on A (ae_restrict_iff' applied to the hypothesis), the integrand u·div g vanishes (volume.restrict A)-a.e., so ∫_A u div g = 0 and the term is ofReal 0 = 0. A supremum of zeros is 0. This proves the first conjunct (for every n).

Case n = 0. E is a single point, so U = E (it contains ξ) and |Du|(E) = |Du|(U). Since C ≥ 1, |Du|(E) ≤ ofReal C·|Du|(U) ≤ ofReal C·(|Du|(U) + ofReal R⁻¹·∫⁻_U ‖u‖ₑ). From now on n ≥ 1, so U ≠ E (U is bounded) and Uᶜ ≠ ∅.
Reduction. If |Du|(U) = ∞, the right side of the second conjunct is ∞, because ofReal C ≠ 0. Assume M_U := (|Du|(U)).toReal with |Du|(U) = ofReal M_U < ∞, and put A_U := ∫_U |u| < ∞ (so ofReal A_U = ∫⁻_U ‖u‖ₑ).

C1. The distance function. d(x) := infDist(x, Uᶜ).
 (a) d is 1-Lipschitz, d = 0 off U, and d > 0 on U (U open).
 (b) d is concave on U. Let x, y ∈ U, t ∈ (0,1), z := (1 − t)x + ty and s := (1 − t)d(x) + t d(y) > 0. Recall ball(x, d(x)) ⊆ U and ball(y, d(y)) ⊆ U. For ‖a‖ < s put a_x := a·d(x)/s and a_y := a·d(y)/s. Then (1 − t)a_x + t a_y = a, ‖a_x‖ < d(x) and ‖a_y‖ < d(y), so z + a = (1 − t)(x + a_x) + t(y + a_y) ∈ U by convexity. Hence ball(z,s) ⊆ U and d(z) ≥ s.
 (c) If x ∈ U and d is differentiable at x, then ‖Dd(x)‖ = 1. Indeed ‖Dd(x)‖ ≤ 1 since d is 1-Lipschitz. Conversely, Uᶜ is closed and nonempty and E is proper, so there is a ∈ Uᶜ with ‖x − a‖ = d(x) > 0 (IsClosed.exists_infDist_eq_dist). With e := (a − x)/‖a − x‖ and 0 ≤ s ≤ d(x), we get d(x + se) ≤ ‖x + se − a‖ = d(x) − s. Hence Dd(x)[e] ≤ −1 and ‖Dd(x)‖ ≥ 1.

C2. Key geometric inequality. Let η₀ := min{d(y) : y ∈ closedBall(ξ,δR)} > 0; this is a continuous positive function on a nonempty compact subset of U. Claim: if x ∈ U, d is differentiable at x and d(x) < η₀, then −Dd(x)[x − ξ] > δR.
 Proof. Let ν ∈ E be the gradient of d at x, so Dd(x)[h] = ⟨ν,h⟩ and ‖ν‖ = 1 by C1(c). Put w := ξ − δRν. Then w ∈ closedBall(ξ,δR) ⊆ U, so d(w) ≥ η₀ > d(x).
 The segment [x,w] lies in U, and φ(t) := d(x + t(w − x)) is concave on [0,1] by C1(b), with φ'(0) = Dd(x)[w − x]. For a concave φ the slope (φ(t) − φ(0))/t is nonincreasing in t ∈ (0,1], so φ(1) − φ(0) ≤ φ'(0). Hence
   0 < d(w) − d(x) ≤ ⟨ν, w − x⟩ = ⟨ν, ξ − x⟩ − δR‖ν‖² = −Dd(x)[x − ξ] − δR.

C3. Cut-offs.
 (a) Null level sets. For c > 0 the level sets {d = c} are pairwise disjoint measurable subsets of U, and μ(U) < ∞. So the set B of c > 0 with μ({d = c}) > 0 is countable (Mathlib Measure.countable_meas_pos_of_disjoint_iUnion). Choose ε_j ∈ (0, min(η₀, 1/(j + 1))) with ε_j ∉ B and ε_j/2 ∉ B; this is possible since the excluded set B ∪ 2B is countable. So ε_j → 0, ε_j < η₀, and μ({d = ε_j}) = μ({d = ε_j/2}) = 0.
 (b) The cut-off. For ε > 0 let γ_ε(t) := min{1, max{0, 2t/ε − 1}}; it is (2/ε)-Lipschitz, takes values in [0,1], equals 0 for t ≤ ε/2 and 1 for t ≥ ε. Put φ_ε := γ_ε ∘ d. Then:
 - φ_ε is (2/ε)-Lipschitz and 0 ≤ φ_ε ≤ 1;
 - φ_ε = 0 on {d ≤ ε/2}, so tsupport φ_ε ⊆ {d ≥ ε/2}, a closed bounded subset of U, hence compact;
 - φ_ε = 1 on {d ≥ ε};
 - φ_ε(x) → 1_U(x) as ε → 0 for every x: for x ∈ U, φ_ε(x) = 1 as soon as ε ≤ d(x); for x ∉ U, d(x) = 0 so φ_ε(x) = 0.
 (c) The a.e. inequality. Fix ε = ε_j and consider the open sets A₁ := {d < ε/2}, A₂ := {ε/2 < d < ε} and A₃ := {d > ε}. They cover E up to the μ-null set {d = ε/2} ∪ {d = ε}.
 - On A₁ and on A₃, φ_ε is locally constant, so Dφ_ε = 0 there.
 - On A₂, φ_ε = (2/ε)d − 1, so at every x ∈ A₂ where d is differentiable (a.e. by Rademacher), Dφ_ε(x) = (2/ε)Dd(x) (derivatives of functions agreeing near x coincide). For such x we have x ∈ U and d(x) < ε < η₀, so C1(c) and C2 give δR‖Dφ_ε(x)‖ = (2/ε)δR ≤ (2/ε)(−Dd(x)[x − ξ]) = −Dφ_ε(x)[x − ξ].
 Hence for μ-a.e. x:
   δR‖Dφ_ε(x)‖ ≤ −Dφ_ε(x)[x − ξ].   (C3)

C4. Key bound: for ε = ε_j, ∫ |u|‖Dφ_ε‖ ≤ δ⁻¹M_U + nδ⁻¹R⁻¹A_U.
 (a) The field V(x) := φ_ε(x)(x − ξ)/R.
 - V is Lipschitz. If φ_ε(x) ≠ 0 then x ∈ U ⊆ closedBall(ξ,R), and V(x) − V(y) = φ_ε(y)(x − y)/R + (φ_ε(x) − φ_ε(y))(x − ξ)/R, so ‖V(x) − V(y)‖ ≤ (1/R + 2/ε)‖x − y‖. The case φ_ε(y) ≠ 0 is symmetric, and if both vanish then V(x) = V(y) = 0.
 - tsupport V ⊆ tsupport φ_ε ⊆ U is compact, and ‖V(x)‖ ≤ φ_ε(x)‖x − ξ‖/R ≤ 1.
 So −V (an element of C_c(E,E)) is admissible for U.
 (b) At every x where φ_ε is differentiable (a.e.), DV(x)[h] = (φ_ε(x)h + Dφ_ε(x)[h](x − ξ))/R, so div V(x) = (nφ_ε(x) + Dφ_ε(x)[x − ξ])/R. Hence a.e. −Dφ_ε(x)[x − ξ] = nφ_ε(x) − R div V(x).
 (c) By (C3), a.e. |u|‖Dφ_ε‖ ≤ (δR)⁻¹|u|(nφ_ε − R div V). All these functions are integrable: u ∈ L¹, and φ_ε, Dφ_ε, div V are bounded and measurable. So
   ∫ |u|‖Dφ_ε‖ ≤ (δR)⁻¹(n∫|u|φ_ε − R∫|u| div V).
 (d) First term: ∫|u|φ_ε ≤ ∫_U |u| = A_U, since 0 ≤ φ_ε ≤ 1_U.
 (e) Second term. div(−V) = −div V everywhere (fderiv(−V) = −fderiv V), and div V = 0 off tsupport V ⊆ U. So
   −∫|u| div V = ∫_U |u| div(−V) ≤ (|D|u||(U)).toReal,
 by ofReal_integral_le_bvVariationOn applied to the function |u| and the admissible field −V. By the sibling theorem Submission.bv_abs_variation_le (O := U open; u is integrable on E, hence locally integrable on U), |D|u||(U) ≤ |Du|(U) = ofReal M_U < ∞. So −∫|u| div V ≤ M_U.
 Therefore ∫|u|‖Dφ_ε‖ ≤ (δR)⁻¹(nA_U + R M_U) = δ⁻¹M_U + nδ⁻¹R⁻¹A_U.

C5. Bound on |Du|(E). Let g be admissible for E = univ, Λ-Lipschitz. By iSup_le it suffices to prove ∫_E u div g ≤ C(M_U + R⁻¹A_U); note ∫ x in univ, … = ∫ x, … (Measure.restrict_univ).
 (a) Dominated convergence. φ_{ε_j} u div g → 1_U u div g pointwise (C3(b)), with dominating function nΛ|u| ∈ L¹. Also 1_U u = u a.e.: u = 0 a.e. off closure U, and closure U ∖ U = frontier U is μ-null for convex U (Mathlib Convex.addHaar_frontier). Hence ∫ u div g = lim_j ∫ φ_{ε_j} u div g.
 (b) Fix j and ε = ε_j.
 - φ_ε g is Lipschitz, being the product of two bounded Lipschitz functions; tsupport(φ_ε g) ⊆ tsupport φ_ε ⊆ U is compact; ‖φ_ε g‖ ≤ 1. So φ_ε g is admissible for U.
 - At every x where both φ_ε and g are differentiable (a.e., Rademacher), D(φ_ε g)(x)[h] = φ_ε(x)Dg(x)[h] + Dφ_ε(x)[h]·g(x). Hence div(φ_ε g)(x) = φ_ε(x) div g(x) + Dφ_ε(x)[g(x)], since the trace of h ↦ Dφ_ε(x)[h]·g(x) is Dφ_ε(x)[g(x)].
 - All integrands are integrable (u ∈ L¹, the other factors bounded measurable). So
   ∫ φ_ε u div g = ∫ u div(φ_ε g) − ∫ u Dφ_ε[g] ≤ ∫_U u div(φ_ε g) + ∫|u|‖Dφ_ε‖,
 using ‖g‖ ≤ 1, and ∫ u div(φ_ε g) = ∫_U u div(φ_ε g) because div(φ_ε g) vanishes off U.
 - Admissibility gives ofReal(∫_U u div(φ_ε g)) ≤ |Du|(U) = ofReal M_U, so ∫_U u div(φ_ε g) ≤ M_U.
 - With C4: ∫ φ_ε u div g ≤ M_U + δ⁻¹M_U + nδ⁻¹R⁻¹A_U ≤ C(M_U + R⁻¹A_U).
 (c) Letting j → ∞ in (a) gives ∫_E u div g ≤ C(M_U + R⁻¹A_U). Since C, M_U, R⁻¹, A_U ≥ 0,
   ofReal(∫_E u div g) ≤ ofReal C·(ofReal M_U + ofReal R⁻¹·ofReal A_U) = ofReal C·(|Du|(U) + ofReal R⁻¹·∫⁻_U ‖u‖ₑ).
 Taking the supremum over g gives bvVariationOn u univ ≤ ofReal C·(bvVariationOn u U + ofReal R⁻¹·∫⁻ x in U, ‖u x‖ₑ). Together with C0 this proves BVExtensionEstimate with C = max(1 + δ⁻¹, nδ⁻¹). ∎
proof_key_steps: C = max(1 + 1/δ, n/δ); C0: |Du|((closure U)ᶜ) = 0 because u = 0 a.e. there; n = 0 trivial; assume |Du|(U) < ∞.
C1–C2: d = dist(·,Uᶜ) is concave on U with |∇d| = 1 where differentiable; the supergradient inequality at w = ξ − δR∇d(x) gives −(x − ξ)·∇d(x) > δR when d(x) < η₀.
C3: choose ε_j ↓ 0 with null level sets; Lipschitz cut-offs φ_ε = γ_ε∘d satisfy δR|∇φ_ε| ≤ −(x − ξ)·∇φ_ε a.e. and φ_ε → 1_U.
C4: with the admissible field −V, V = φ_ε(x − ξ)/R, and Submission.bv_abs_variation_le, get ∫|u||∇φ_ε| ≤ δ⁻¹|Du|(U) + nδ⁻¹R⁻¹∫_U|u|.

C5: for each test field g, the a.e. product rule div(φ_ε g) = φ_ε div g + ∇φ_ε·g, admissibility of φ_ε g for U, C4, and dominated convergence (frontier of convex U is null) give ∫u div g ≤ C(|Du|(U) + R⁻¹∫_U|u|).
